cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Ethics & Sustainability
cards.back: Engineering ethics guides decision-making when commercial, safety and environmental interests conflict.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Ethics & Sustainability
cards.back: The 6 Rs of sustainability: Rethink, Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Repair - applied in order of preference.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Ethics & Sustainability
cards.back: Cradle-to-grave analysis considers environmental impact from raw material extraction to final disposal.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Ethics & Sustainability
cards.back: Cradle-to-cradle (circular economy) design aims for products to be fully recycled or composted, eliminating waste.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Ethics & Sustainability
cards.back: Eco-design integrates environmental considerations into every stage of the product development process.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Ethics & Sustainability
cards.back: Renewable energy sources reduce dependence on fossil fuels and lower carbon emissions.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Ethics & Sustainability
cards.back: Designing for disassembly allows products to be taken apart easily at end of life for recycling.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Ethics & Sustainability
cards.back: Engineers must balance competing demands: cost, performance, safety, environmental impact and social responsibility.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Ethics & Sustainability
cards.back: Whistleblowing reports unsafe or unethical practices; engineers have a duty to report serious safety concerns.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Ethics & Sustainability
cards.back: Planned obsolescence conflicts with sustainability: designing products to fail encourages waste.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Ethics & Sustainability
cards.back: Carbon footprint measures total greenhouse gas emissions caused by a product or organisation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Ethics & Sustainability
cards.back: Sustainable materials are sourced responsibly: certified timber, recycled metals and bio-based polymers.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse engineering exam tips — engineering ethics & sustainability?
cards.back: 1. For Engineering Ethics & Sustainability questions, use precise design and technology terminology 2. Consider function, aesthetics, ergonomics, sustainability and cost in your answers 3. When evaluating, justify your design decisions with reference to user needs and specifications 4. Show your understanding of Engineering Ethics & Sustainability through both theory and practical application 5. Reference real products and manufacturing processes where relevant
